source.title: With Greater Distance Comes Worse Performance: On the Perspective of Layer Utilization and Model Generalization

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The paper’s results are mainly in figures; exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies the fraction of shuffled training labels and reports generalization and resilience results, but its results qualify the claim: the authors describe better recovery of correct labels in some overparameterized models, and their resilience measure differs from test error.
record.gate_note: The paper studies fully connected networks trained on MNIST and CIFAR10 with shuffled-label fractions. It does not report a direct experiment with a completely random labeling and chance test error, shuffled or Gaussian-noise inputs, regularization comparisons, or training-time comparisons. Figure-only heatmaps cover multiple model sizes and noise ratios, whose individual values cannot be reliably transcribed from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own results on fitting corrupted training labels across network capacities, bearing on V4's training-fit component. It does not establish smooth test-error degradation or fitting completely random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. Early layers contribute broadly useful information, while deeper layers increasingly capture noise and can harm testing loss and resilience. The authors propose deeper-layer distance from initialization as an indicator of generalization and report that resetting final layers can reduce overfit. These layer results do not establish a temporal real-label-first learning sequence.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses fully connected networks trained on MNIST and CIFAR10, varies hidden-layer size and the fraction of shuffled labels, and measures generalization and resilience. It does not reproduce the original random-label experiment as stated in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, hidden-layer size, and shuffled-label fraction affect the reported patterns; the text notes that CIFAR10’s greater complexity leaves more models underparameterized under the chosen size range.

fits_no_version.finding: Recovered-label loss exhibits double descent and remains worse in models that memorize shuffled labels, with some improvement beyond the interpolation threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recovery of original labels on corrupted training examples depends on network capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: Deeper layers contribute more as corruption increases and can harm testing loss; reinitializing them can reduce overfit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalizable information and memorized noise have different layer contributions after training.

record.problems: Results relevant to label corruption are primarily figure-only, with no exact plotted values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. The experiments use fully connected networks only. The authors note uncertainty in measuring convergence of testing loss.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were left out; figure-only results are retained as aggregate dataset rows because the supplied text does not provide recoverable condition-level values.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero or near-zero training error at that endpoint, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to clean-label training are not established.
Relative training time and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A readable corruption sweep establishing perfect training fit throughout and steadily rising held-out test error toward chance. Exact corruption endpoints are unavailable.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation, including generalization after removing them.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noise. Layer contributions after training do not establish that ordering.

missing.what: Separate qualitative training-fit results by capacity: low or close-to-perfect training risk in overparameterized models, versus failure to achieve close-to-perfect fit in underparameterized models. Exact errors and corruption endpoints are not supplied.

record.verdict_notes: The original limits_scope verdict based on diagonal heatmap patterns and resilience is unsupported: neither establishes a failure of smooth test-error degradation. The replacement verdicts concern only the explicitly reported training-fit component. All models were trained for 10000 epochs; testing-loss convergence remains uncertain.

versions.untested_parts: The paper varies shuffled-label fractions, but does not state results for completely random labels with test error at chance or establish that architecture and hyperparameters were unchanged relative to a true-label comparison.
Training time and convergence slowdown as corruption increases are not reported.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
The paper reports generalization as the train/test risk gap and resilience on recovered labels, not test error itself; the supplied text does not give exact plotted values for each noise fraction.
No weight-decay, dropout, or data-augmentation comparisons are reported.
The paper discusses early and deeper layer contributions, but does not compare learning patterns over training time for real versus random labels.
